ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ (١) الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ (٢) يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ (٣)).
The «hāʾ» [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa] in «الْهُمَزَة» and «اللُّمَزَة» is for intensification (mubālagha).
(الَّذِي) may be genitive as a badal (substitute), accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean), or nominative on [the implied] «هُوَ» (he is).
(عَدَّدَهُ) is with a doubled consonant, as a verb, either from «الْعَدَد» (counting) or from «الْإِعْدَاد» (preparing).
(يَحْسَبُ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «جَمَعَ». (أَخْلَدَهُ) is in the sense of «يُخَلِّدُهُ» (will make him immortal). It is also said that it is in its proper sense, i.e. it lengthened his life.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (لَيُنْبَذَنَّ): i.e. the one who amasses. [It is also read] «لَيُنْبَذَانِّ», i.e. he and his wealth; and «لَيُنْبَذُنَّ» with a ḍamma on the dhāl, i.e. he, his wealth and his counting [of it] as well; and it may be that the meaning is he and his various kinds of wealth, because they are diverse.

ukberi-tibyan:6-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ (٦) الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ (٧) إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ (٨) فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ (٩)).
The words of the Exalted (نَارُ اللَّهِ): i.e. «هِيَ نَارُ اللَّهِ» (it is the fire of Allah). (الَّتِي) is nominative as a naʿt (adjective), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or in the position of the accusative by «أَعْنِي» (I mean).
(الْأَفْئِدَةِ) is a plural of paucity (jamʿ qilla) used in place of [a plural of] multitude. «الْعَمَد» with a fatḥa is the plural of «عَمُود» or «عِمَاد» (pillar), and it is a rare plural.
It is said that it is also read with two ḍammas, like «كِتَاب» and «كُتُب», «رَسُول» and «رُسُل». The implied form is: «هُمْ فِي عَمَدٍ» (they are in pillars). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun, i.e. bound fast; and it may be a ṣifa (adjective) of «مُؤْصَدَة». And Allah knows best.
